events.text: The clerk has a petition ready to file, except that the names and the request still need checking. You could help prepare it and explain the corrections. If the work is accepted, the clerk may recommend you for royal service.

choices.text: Help prepare the petition

outcomes.text: You check the names, rewrite the request and answer the clerk's questions. The clerk agrees to recommend you. You still need the skills and age required for a court appointment.

weightModifiers.reason: Your household knows written accounts
Practised writing
Experience explaining requests
Your current work uses written records
You have presented a district petition
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: The clerk corrects several passages and files the petition. No recommendation follows. You are paid for the copying.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: The list and the stores disagree
events.text: Your unit's equipment list does not explain everything in the stores. An officer wants the shortages made clear before the next issue. You could take the count in hand and explain the revised account.

choices.text: Take charge of the supply lists

outcomes.text: The records match the stores, and your officer accepts the revised list. They agree to recommend you for more responsibility. This helps future applications; it does not change your rank.

weightModifiers.reason: Household experience with lists and accounts
You can check supply totals
You understand the unit's equipment
You can explain the shortages
You have wartime supply experience
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: You find missing entries, but another soldier has to help finish the count. You return to ordinary duties with more practice.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: Your calculations beside the reader's
events.text: An experienced reader is checking copied sky tables for a paying household. There is space beside the working copy for your own calculations. Showing them could earn a recommendation for a regular post.

choices.text: Show your copied tables and calculations

outcomes.text: The reader checks your arithmetic and offers to recommend you to the paying household. A regular post is open once you meet its skill requirements. You keep your current work until you accept it.

weightModifiers.reason: Household experience with writing and accounts
You have practised sky-table work
Your arithmetic is well practised
Your current work involves written records
You have completed a paid sky-table copy
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: The reader points out a copied position and a calculation to correct. There is no work offer, but you leave with useful corrections.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: A sample for the larger order
events.text: A customer brings an order too large for the usual hurried arrangement at the bench. They want someone who can finish the work and organise the smaller tasks. Your pottery, carving or sculpture could serve as the sample.

choices.text: Show a finished piece and explain the work

outcomes.text: The customer accepts your sample and recommends you to a workshop owner. You can apply to lead work in your trained trade once you meet the requirements. You keep your current job for now.

weightModifiers.reason: Your household has workshop contacts
You have an experienced specialism
You already work in a skilled workshop
You have completed a paid craft order
You can explain quantities and costs
Illness or injury makes the extra work harder
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: The customer asks for a different finish and places the larger order elsewhere. You correct the sample and sell it as an ordinary piece.

choices.text: Keep to your usual work

outcomes.text: You leave the extra task to someone else and keep to your usual work.

events.title: Ready cash across the table
events.text: The moneylender sets ready cash within reach and names the repayment terms. You would have to repay this loan yourself. An unpaid balance can bring collectors, assault and, after a long delay, a fatal confrontation.

choices.text: Turn down the loan

outcomes.text: You turn down the loan. You owe this lender nothing.

choices.text: Borrow from the moneylender — dangerous loan

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's cash and repayment terms. You must pay this loan yourself. If it stays unpaid after the deadline, the collectors can threaten, injure or kill you.

events.title: The repayment day has come
events.text: The moneylender opens the account at your name and asks for the remaining balance. The agreed deadline has arrived. Leaving it unpaid can bring threats and, with a longer delay, a dangerous confrontation.

choices.text: Pay the remaining balance

outcomes.text: You pay the remaining balance. The lender marks the loan settled. You owe them nothing.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas toward the loan

outcomes.text: You pay 10 drachmas toward the loan. The remaining balance keeps its existing deadline.

choices.text: Ask for an extension

outcomes.text: The lender adds the agreed extension charge to the balance and gives you a new deadline.

choices.text: Leave the loan unpaid for now

outcomes.text: You leave the balance unpaid. The deadline has not changed, and the collectors may return.

events.title: Two men at the doorway
events.text: Two collectors stand in your doorway and ask for the overdue balance. They say the next visit will be rougher if you keep delaying. Their warning changes neither the amount owed nor its deadline.

choices.text: Pay the remaining balance

outcomes.text: You pay the remaining balance. The lender marks the loan settled. You owe them nothing.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas toward the loan

outcomes.text: You pay 10 drachmas toward the loan. The remaining balance keeps its existing deadline.

choices.text: Ask for an extension

outcomes.text: The lender adds the agreed extension charge to the balance and gives you a new deadline.

choices.text: Leave the loan unpaid for now

outcomes.text: You leave the balance unpaid. The deadline has not changed, and the collectors may return.

events.title: No room to pass
events.text: The collectors stop you on the way home and leave no clear space to pass. The loan has been overdue for years, and they threaten violence unless you settle it. Running or refusing can end in a fatal wound.

choices.text: Pay the remaining balance

outcomes.text: You pay the remaining balance. The lender marks the loan settled. You owe them nothing.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas toward the loan

outcomes.text: You pay 10 drachmas toward the loan. The remaining balance keeps its existing deadline.

choices.text: Ask for an extension

outcomes.text: The lender adds the agreed extension charge to the balance and gives you a new deadline.

choices.text: Ask the neighbors to speak for you

outcomes.text: Neighbors speak with the collectors. They leave without hurting you, but the balance remains overdue.

weightModifiers.reason: People nearby are willing to speak for you
You can explain your request clearly

outcomes.text: The collectors shove your neighbors aside and beat you before leaving. You are hurt, and the loan remains unpaid.
A collector strikes your lower leg. You suffer an open tibial fracture and need care. The loan remains unpaid.

choices.text: Try to get past them and run

outcomes.text: You get past the collectors and reach a crowded street. You escape for now, but the loan is still overdue.
A collector catches you and strikes your lower leg. You suffer an open tibial fracture and need care.
A collector stabs you in the chest as you try to pass. The wound proves fatal.

choices.text: Refuse to pay or go with them

outcomes.text: The collectors beat you and leave. You are badly hurt, and the loan remains overdue.
The collectors strike your lower leg. An open tibial fracture stops you walking, and you need care.
A collector stabs you in the chest during the confrontation. The wound proves fatal.

events.title: A different sleeping place
events.text: Your household moves your sleeping basket away from a draft. You wake in the unfamiliar corner and cry until someone picks you up.

events.title: Across the mat
events.text: You cross a mat toward the doorway. An adult moves a basket out of your path and calls you back from the street.

events.title: A lid on the floor
events.text: Someone leaves a pot lid within reach. You bang it against the floor until the cook trades it for a wooden spoon.

events.title: The cat keeps its distance
events.text: You reach for a cat resting near the wall. It moves out of reach and watches you from a shelf.

events.title: Supper on a lap
events.text: A relative keeps you on their lap through supper. You take food from their bowl and fall asleep before the dishes are cleared.

events.title: A cloth to hold
events.text: While someone washes you, they let you hold the clean cloth. You drop it into the water and laugh at the splash.

events.title: Waiting out the rain
events.text: Rain keeps the household indoors. Someone moves a basket so you have room to crawl while the adults finish their work.

events.title: A bark at the door
events.text: A dog barks outside the doorway. You hurry back to a familiar adult and watch it from behind their legs.

events.title: A restless night
events.text: You will not settle to sleep. The adults take turns carrying you until the room finally becomes quiet.

events.title: Stones in a bowl
events.text: A relative gives you a bowl and a few smooth stones. You move them in and out while they keep count aloud.

events.title: Sandals that slip
events.text: Your household fits a pair of small sandals to your feet. You keep kicking one off, and someone keeps putting it back.

events.title: Behind the hanging cloth
events.text: An older child hides behind a hanging cloth and calls your name. You pull the edge aside each time they disappear.

events.title: Holding the cup
events.text: Someone helps you drink from a small cup. Most reaches your mouth, and the rest runs down the front of your clothes.

events.title: An afternoon with a relative
events.text: The usual carer has an errand. A relative looks after you, learning which song and which toy will keep you settled.

events.title: Two similar baskets
events.text: You bring home the wrong basket from an errand. An adult goes back with you, and the shopkeeper swaps it for the right one.

events.title: A game with seeds
events.text: Children mark a game on the ground and use seeds as counters. You argue over a move, erase the lines and start again.

events.title: A scrap sail
events.text: You tie a scrap of cloth to a stick and float it in a shallow basin. The little boat tips over as soon as you let go.

events.title: Under the bench
events.text: A chick slips into the room. You crouch under a bench to catch it while its owner waits at the door.

events.title: Pits to sort
events.text: After a meal, you sort olive pits into neat rows. Someone sweeps them into a bowl before the next task can begin.

events.title: A faded doorway mark
events.text: You use a mark on a wall to remember a turning. When the wall is patched, you have to learn another way to recognize the street.

events.title: The bread is still warm
events.text: You carry a loaf home wrapped in cloth. You keep switching hands because the bread is hotter than you expected.

events.title: A strap comes loose
events.text: The strap on a small jug slips from its knot. You set the jug down and wait for someone to retie it before carrying on.

events.title: A shelf to clear
events.text: An adult asks you to clear the bottom shelf of a storeroom. You find a missing spoon behind the jars.

events.title: Getting the words wrong
events.text: You try to join a song in the courtyard. Another child quietly teaches you the words you keep missing.

events.title: Following the shade
events.text: You trace the edge of a building's shade on the ground. Later, you come back and find the line has moved.

events.title: A bead in the dust
events.text: A loose bead rolls between the floor stones. You work it out with a thin stick and return it to its owner.

events.title: Watching the scales
events.text: You stand beside an adult while a seller weighs a purchase. On the way home, they explain why they watched both sides of the scales.

events.title: Remembering a visitor's name
events.text: A visitor asks if you remember them. You remember the food they brought last time, but need help with the name.

events.title: Before the street fills
events.text: You leave early to finish an errand before the street gets busy. The shop has not opened, so you wait with the other early arrivals.

events.title: A knot that holds
events.text: Someone checks the knot on a bundle you tied. They undo it, show you another turn and ask you to try again.

events.title: Two people with the same name
events.text: You deliver a message to the wrong person with the right name. They point you toward the other household before you walk away.

events.title: A handle needs wrapping
events.text: A tool handle is rubbing your palm. You wrap it with a strip of cloth and finish the small job more comfortably.

events.title: A late supper
events.text: A task runs past the meal hour. Your household saves a portion and asks what kept you when you finally arrive.

events.title: Remembering the price
events.text: You repeat the agreed price while walking to make a purchase. At the stall, you remember it but have to count the coins twice.

events.title: Carrying it together
events.text: A bundle is awkward rather than heavy. Another young worker takes the far end, and the two of you get it through the doorway.

events.title: The yard fills again
events.text: You finish sweeping a work yard just before a delivery arrives. Loose packing covers the clean ground, and you fetch the broom again.

events.title: A contest with no prize
events.text: A group challenges each other to balance a pebble on a narrow post. Nobody manages it for long, and no money changes hands.

events.title: Keeping an offcut
events.text: A worker lets you keep a small offcut after clearing the bench. You bring it home and use it to wedge a loose shutter.

events.title: Checking before leaving
events.text: You return to check a delivery before leaving the yard. One item is missing, and you find it where the cart was unloaded.

events.title: A message over the noise
events.text: You try to call a message across a noisy street. Nobody hears the whole thing, so you walk over and say it again.

events.title: The lamp goes out
events.text: The lamp runs out of oil in the middle of an evening task. You leave the last part until daylight.

events.title: Checking a payment mark
events.text: A household payment is questioned. You find the mark recording the earlier payment and settle the mistake without paying again.

events.title: A split bag
events.text: A bag splits on the way home. You borrow a bowl from a nearby stall, gather what you can and return the bowl before supper.

events.title: A cart blocks the lane
events.text: A cart with a damaged wheel blocks your lane. The people carrying goods pass them around it until the owner clears the way.

events.title: Washing on the line
events.text: A line holding washed clothes sags into the dust. You take the clothes down, tighten the rope and rinse the fallen pieces again.

events.title: Waiting for your turn
events.text: You arrive to collect water just as several other households do. Everyone waits while a cracked vessel is moved out of the way.

events.title: No smaller coins
events.text: A seller cannot make change for your purchase. You visit another stall for a small item and come back with a more useful set of coins.

events.title: Returning a pan
events.text: A neighbor brings back a borrowed pan with food still in it. You share the food and remember to return their bowl the next day.

events.title: A loaf for tomorrow
events.text: A loaf has gone too dry to eat on its own. You soften pieces in a bowl rather than throw it away.

events.title: A reed catches your foot
events.text: A loose reed is sticking out of the sleeping mat. You trim it and turn the worn edge toward the wall.

events.title: The seller has moved
events.text: You go to the usual place for a purchase and find a different seller. Someone points you to the stall you were looking for.

events.title: Room on the bench
events.text: A visitor arrives while the room is being used for work. You clear a place on a bench and move the tools back after they leave.

events.title: More onions than planned
events.text: A household purchase turns out larger than expected. You swap part of it with a neighbor before the food spoils.

events.title: A rattling shutter
events.text: A shutter keeps knocking in the wind. You find its loose pin and secure it with a small wooden wedge.

events.title: A dark stair
events.text: You pause at an unlit stair until someone brings a lamp. The wait is shorter than feeling your way down with a full basket.

events.title: Keeping flies off the food
events.text: You spend part of a meal chasing flies away. Before the next meal, you find a cloth wide enough to cover the serving bowl.

events.title: A shorter round of errands
events.text: You combine two nearby errands and leave the farther one for another day. The household still has what it needs for supper.

events.title: Moving the seat
events.text: You move a seat nearer the doorway for better light. Someone objects to the narrow passage, and you find a place that suits you both.

events.title: Explaining the recipe
events.text: A younger person asks how you prepare a familiar dish. You give the quantities, then have to explain what you mean by a small handful.

events.title: A lid for an old jar
events.text: The lid of an old storage jar no longer fits well. You test two others before finding one that keeps the contents covered.

events.title: The visitor is late
events.text: A visitor arrives long after the agreed time. You have already eaten, so you put out a small plate while they explain the delay.

events.title: Trying a nearer shop
events.text: You try a shop closer to home. The choice is smaller, but the shorter walk makes it useful for ordinary purchases.

events.title: Sorting a tangle of cord
events.text: You sit down with a tangled bundle of cord. By the time someone asks for a length, you have enough of it untangled to help.

events.title: The streets have changed
events.text: You give someone directions, then remember that a passage has been closed. You call them back before they turn the corner.

events.title: Something from an old household task
events.text: You find a small item left from an old household task. You explain what it was used for before putting it back with the other things.

events.title: Taking the lighter basket
events.text: Two baskets need carrying. You take the lighter one and agree where to meet the person carrying the other.

events.title: Listening at the doorway
events.text: You sit by the doorway while people discuss a delivery. You recognize the place they mention and settle a disagreement about the route.

events.title: A useful measure
events.text: A household measure has lost its handle. You show someone which unbroken cup can hold the same amount until it is repaired.

events.title: Balancing the load
events.text: A load keeps slipping to one side. You stop, move the packing and ask another porter to check it before setting off.

events.title: An unclear cargo mark
events.text: Two bundles have similar cargo marks. You leave them apart until the person receiving the delivery identifies the right one.

events.title: Pots drying too quickly
events.text: The edges of a fresh clay piece are drying faster than its base. You cover part of it and return to check it later.

events.title: Finding space for the firing
events.text: You rearrange a group of dry pots so they will fit the available kiln space. A narrow piece needs a place of its own.

events.title: Following the wood grain
events.text: A cut starts to lift a splinter along the wood grain. You turn the piece and work back from the other direction.

events.title: Matching two fittings
events.text: Two wooden fittings are meant to match. You set them side by side and remove a little more from the uneven one.

events.title: Checking the relief in daylight
events.text: A shallow line in the stone disappears when you move the lamp. You check the relief in daylight before deciding whether it needs another cut.

events.title: A total checked twice
events.text: You check a column of quantities and get two different totals. A line was counted twice; you correct it before the record is handed over.

events.title: Keeping a sheet dry
events.text: Water reaches the edge of the workbench. You lift the written sheet clear and dry the bench before continuing the copy.

events.title: Moving the display
events.text: A doorway display keeps getting knocked by people passing. You move it farther inside and leave more room to enter.

events.title: A coil out of place
events.text: A loose coil of rope is lying where the crew walks. You put it away before the next load comes aboard.

events.title: Waiting ashore
events.text: The crew is ready before the cargo is. You wait ashore and check the bundles when the last delivery finally arrives.

events.title: A different example
events.text: A learner cannot follow an argument. You try an example about buying bread, and they can finally explain the point back to you.

events.title: A line copied out of place
events.text: A copied sky table has one line shifted into the wrong column. You compare it with the source and mark where the copy must be corrected.

events.title: A client asks again
events.text: A client asks you to repeat part of a traditional sky-omen reading. You explain what the tradition claims and where observation does not support a definite answer.

events.title: Checking the kit
events.text: You spread out your equipment and replace a worn fastening. Another soldier points out a strap you had missed.

events.title: The supply tally
events.text: The supply tally does not match the delivered bundles. You have the bundles opened and counted before accepting the delivery.

events.title: Waiting outside the meeting
events.text: A meeting runs late. You compare notes with another attendant and check which papers you will need when called inside.

events.title: A visit cut short
events.text: You meet the person you are courting, but a household errand cuts the visit short. You agree on another time before leaving.

events.title: A small thing remembered
events.text: The person you are courting brings something you mentioned needing. You had forgotten the conversation, but they had remembered it.

events.title: Keeping supper warm
events.text: One of you comes home late. The other keeps part of supper covered, and you catch up while the dishes are put away.

events.title: Making room for two tasks
events.text: You and your spouse both need the same work surface. You move one task to a tray and finish without another argument.

events.title: Another question
events.text: A child in your household asks why the moon does not look the same every night. You watch it together and answer what you can.

events.title: Sandals left in the way
events.text: A child leaves sandals where everyone walks. After someone trips over them, you find a place where the child can put them each day.

events.title: Help without being asked
events.text: One of your children helps put away the meal without being asked. The job goes faster, though a bowl ends up on the wrong shelf.

events.title: A bundle returned
events.text: After the separation, a bundle of your things reaches your household. You check it and send back an item that belongs to your former spouse.

events.title: A place at someone else's meal
events.text: A neighbor invites you to a meal with their household. You bring a small contribution and stay to help clear the dishes.

events.title: News carried by a relative
events.text: A relative brings household news from across the neighborhood. You ask them to take a short reply when they next visit.

events.title: A jar breaks on your errand
events.text: A small empty jar slips from your hands. Nobody saw it fall, and the household will ask where it is.

choices.text: Tell the household what happened

outcomes.text: You show the broken pieces. An adult helps you clear them and sends you with an unbroken jar next time.

choices.text: Ask someone to show you a repair

outcomes.text: The jar will not hold water again, but a worker shows you how to secure the pieces for another use.

choices.text: Hide the pieces for now

outcomes.text: The missing jar is noticed. You have to explain the breakage and why you hid it.

events.title: An argument over the game
events.text: The children disagree about where the playing area ends. The argument is taking longer than the game.

choices.text: Draw clear lines and start again

outcomes.text: You draw new boundaries where everyone can see them. The game starts over with less arguing.

choices.text: Ask each child to explain their rule

outcomes.text: You hear several different rules. The group agrees on one version for this afternoon.

choices.text: Find something else to do

outcomes.text: You leave the game and spend the afternoon near home. The others are still arguing when you pass later.

events.title: The water is too heavy
events.text: You are asked to carry a small water jar. It is full enough that you keep spilling some as you walk.

choices.text: Ask for a smaller load

outcomes.text: An adult pours some water into another vessel. You carry the lighter jar home without losing more.

choices.text: Ask another child to carry it with you

outcomes.text: You and another child hold the jar between you. You have to agree on each turn, but the water reaches home.

choices.text: Carry it slowly on your own

outcomes.text: You stop several times to change hands. By the time you arrive, the jar is lighter and your arms are tired.

events.title: Clay left on the bench
events.text: A potter lets you use a little leftover clay while an adult watches. There is time for one small piece.

choices.text: Try shaping a tiny cup

outcomes.text: You pinch up the sides of a small cup. The rim is uneven, and the potter shows you where you made it too thin.

choices.text: Make counters for a game

outcomes.text: You roll the clay into small counters and press a mark into each one. The other children help you count them.

choices.text: Watch the potter instead

outcomes.text: You leave the clay alone and watch how the potter keeps the sides of a vessel even.

events.title: Part of the message is missing
events.text: Halfway through an errand, you realize you cannot remember the end of the message.

choices.text: Go back and ask again

outcomes.text: The sender repeats the message. You say it back before setting off a second time.

choices.text: Ask a familiar adult to come with you

outcomes.text: A familiar adult walks back with you and helps you check the message before you deliver it.

choices.text: Deliver only the part you remember

outcomes.text: The recipient has questions you cannot answer. An adult must make another trip to put the message right.

events.title: Your measurements do not match
events.text: You help measure a length of material. Your result differs from the worker checking it.

choices.text: Measure it together from the same end

outcomes.text: You had started from a different mark. Measuring together shows where the difference came from.

choices.text: Practise marking a spare piece

outcomes.text: You practise on a spare piece until the marks line up with the worker's measure.

choices.text: Let the worker finish the measuring

outcomes.text: The worker finishes the measurements while you clear the space for the next task.

events.title: A small payment of your own
events.text: You receive 5 drachmas for a completed errand. Someone at home asks what you plan to do with it.

choices.text: Keep the 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You put the payment away and check where you have stored it before leaving the room.

choices.text: Use the payment for a shared meal

outcomes.text: You bring home food bought with the errand payment. There is a little more to share at supper.

choices.text: Trade the payment for help with numbers

outcomes.text: A worker spends time checking simple sums with you in exchange for the payment.

events.title: A delivery before closing
events.text: Someone offers you 5 drachmas to deliver a small parcel before a nearby shop closes. It will use the time you meant to spend practising.

choices.text: Make the delivery for 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You arrive before the shop closes and bring back the acknowledgment. The sender pays you 5 drachmas.

choices.text: Keep the time for tool practice

outcomes.text: Someone else takes the parcel. You use the time to practise making a clean cut under a worker's eye.

choices.text: Ask a friend to make the trip with you

outcomes.text: Your friend helps you finish the delivery. You share the payment and spend it together on food.

events.title: A chipped measuring cup
events.text: A measuring cup has a chipped rim. You are about to use it for a household purchase.

choices.text: Borrow an unbroken measure

outcomes.text: You borrow a sound measure and check the purchase with it before returning it.

choices.text: Ask how much the damage changes it

outcomes.text: A worker compares the damaged cup with another. You learn why filling it to the chipped rim gives a different amount.

choices.text: Take it back and ask for another

outcomes.text: The household gives you another cup. The errand takes longer, but there is no argument about the quantity.

events.title: A customer you cannot understand
events.text: A customer asks a question in words you do not follow. They point at the goods and begin again.

choices.text: Find someone who understands them

outcomes.text: A nearby worker explains the request. You stay to hear the answer and recognize a few words the next time.

choices.text: Show the goods and check by gesture

outcomes.text: You set out the possible items and let the customer indicate what they need. A worker checks before anything is sold.

choices.text: Leave the request to an experienced worker

outcomes.text: An experienced worker takes over while you return to the task you were doing.

events.title: Room for a neighbor's goods
events.text: A neighbor asks to keep a few dry baskets in your household's storage space for a short time.

choices.text: Make room without charging

outcomes.text: You move your household's baskets together and make space. The neighbor collects everything on the agreed day.

choices.text: Agree on a 5-drachma storage payment

outcomes.text: You agree on which baskets can stay and for how long. The neighbor pays 5 drachmas when collecting them.

choices.text: Keep the space for your own household

outcomes.text: The neighbor finds another place. You keep the storage area ready for your own deliveries.

events.title: Too much change
events.text: After a purchase, you find that the seller returned 5 drachmas more than you were owed.

choices.text: Return the extra coins

outcomes.text: You go back and show the seller the mistake. They check the payment and thank you.

choices.text: Keep the extra coins

outcomes.text: You put the extra coins away. On a later visit, the seller questions the earlier payment.

events.title: The wrong bundle arrives
events.text: A delivery to your household contains goods meant for someone else. The person who brought it has already left.

choices.text: Find the carrier and exchange the bundle

outcomes.text: You find the carrier before the next delivery is unloaded. The two bundles are exchanged.

choices.text: Ask a reader to check the delivery mark

outcomes.text: A reader identifies the household named on the bundle. You take it there and ask where your own delivery went.

choices.text: Keep it aside for the carrier's return

outcomes.text: You leave the bundle unopened. The carrier comes back after the other household notices the mistake.

events.title: A repair does not hold
events.text: A customer returns a small wooden fitting you repaired. The joint has opened, and they want you to put it right.

choices.text: Redo the joint without another charge

outcomes.text: You take the joint apart and make a better fit. The customer checks it before leaving.

choices.text: Return 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You return 5 drachmas and take the fitting back. You examine the failed joint before deciding whether to reuse the wood.

choices.text: Ask a more experienced worker to inspect it

outcomes.text: The worker points out where the wood was split. You explain the fault to the customer and agree on a replacement.

events.title: A relative wants help at a stall
events.text: A relative is trying a small market stall and asks you to help for an afternoon.

choices.text: Help without taking a share

outcomes.text: You watch the goods while your relative handles customers. They finish the afternoon with the stock in order.

choices.text: Check the stock and payment records

outcomes.text: You help count the remaining goods and match the payments. A missed entry explains the uneven total.

choices.text: Keep the time for your own household

outcomes.text: Your relative finds other help. You finish the tasks already waiting at home.

events.title: A joint purchase of grain
events.text: Several neighbors want to combine a grain purchase. Your share would cost 10 drachmas and needs someone to check the quantities.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas and help divide it

outcomes.text: You contribute 10 drachmas and help measure each household's share. Everyone leaves with the agreed amount.

choices.text: Help check the measure without joining

outcomes.text: You help compare the measures before the grain is divided. The neighbors thank you and keep the shares separate.

choices.text: Keep buying for your own household

outcomes.text: You leave the shared purchase to the neighbors and keep to your usual food arrangement.

events.title: A hinge still needs fitting
events.text: You have promised to fit a wooden hinge for someone nearby. Another task has used most of the time you set aside.

choices.text: Finish the fitting before going home

outcomes.text: You check the hinge against the opening and finish it before leaving. The extra work makes for a late meal.

choices.text: Explain the delay and agree on another time

outcomes.text: You tell the household before they start waiting for you. They agree to the new time.

choices.text: Ask another worker to finish it

outcomes.text: Another worker can finish the fitting. You pass over your measurements and leave the rest of the task to them.

events.title: A payment arrives late
events.text: Someone who owes you 10 drachmas for a small job says they cannot pay the whole amount today.

choices.text: Accept 5 drachmas and leave the rest for later

outcomes.text: They pay 5 drachmas now. You agree that the remaining amount is still owed.

choices.text: Accept useful household goods instead

outcomes.text: You agree on goods your household needs and settle the payment that way. The next meal takes less preparation.

choices.text: Agree on a later collection day

outcomes.text: You leave without payment and agree when to return. You keep a note of the amount so there is no dispute later.

events.title: Different plans for the visit
events.text: You and the person you are courting have made different plans for the same free afternoon.

choices.text: Join the visit they planned

outcomes.text: You go with their plan and help carry something for the visit. You have time to talk on the return walk.

choices.text: Choose another time together

outcomes.text: You compare the errands each of you must finish and find a time that works for both.

choices.text: Keep your own plan this time

outcomes.text: You keep the afternoon for your own plans. The other person is disappointed, but the disagreement stays small.

events.title: Two uses for the same coins
events.text: You and your spouse disagree about whether spare cash should go toward supplies or a shared meal with relatives.

choices.text: Check the household supplies together

outcomes.text: You go through what is left before deciding. The discussion settles which purchases can wait.

choices.text: Spend 5 drachmas on a smaller shared meal

outcomes.text: You agree on a smaller meal and spend 5 drachmas. There is still time to talk after the visitors arrive.

choices.text: Leave the coins untouched for now

outcomes.text: You postpone the purchase and the meal. The money stays available, though the decision still needs to be made.

events.title: A child asks about letters
events.text: One of your children asks you to explain marks on a delivered message. You have a little time before the next task.

choices.text: Ask a familiar reader to explain them

outcomes.text: A reader explains a few marks with you both listening. The child repeats them on the way home.

choices.text: Show the child the marks you know

outcomes.text: You explain the marks you recognize and leave the unfamiliar ones for someone who knows more.

choices.text: Finish the household task first

outcomes.text: You put the message somewhere safe and finish the task. The child goes back to playing nearby.

events.title: A child wants to help with work
events.text: One of your children asks for a task while you are arranging materials. There are safe small jobs, but they will need watching.

choices.text: Let the child sort harmless scraps nearby

outcomes.text: You set aside small safe pieces to sort and keep the tools out of reach. You check the piles together when the child finishes.

choices.text: Explain the task without having them do it

outcomes.text: You show the finished pieces and explain what each part does. The child asks more questions than you expected.

choices.text: Keep the work area clear today

outcomes.text: You explain that the task needs your full attention. The child finds another place to play.

events.title: A shared possession after separation
events.text: A household item was left between you and your former spouse. A relative asks you to settle who will keep it.

choices.text: Send it to your former spouse

outcomes.text: You send the item with the relative and ask for an acknowledgment that it arrived.

choices.text: Arrange a practical agreement

outcomes.text: You send a clear account of which items each household still needs. The relative helps carry the reply.

choices.text: Keep it set aside until you can agree

outcomes.text: You leave the item unused and separate from the rest of your things. The question remains open.

events.title: A customer wants a different pattern
events.text: A customer changes the painted pattern after you have prepared a group of clay vessels. The pieces have not yet been fired.

choices.text: Redo the pattern on the agreed pieces

outcomes.text: You remove the unfinished decoration and paint the new pattern. The extra work gives you more practice, but delays the batch.

choices.text: Make a sample before changing the batch

outcomes.text: You paint one sample and show it to the customer. You agree which details to keep before starting the rest.

choices.text: Offer the original pattern as agreed

outcomes.text: You show the original sample and explain what was agreed. The customer accepts it rather than wait for a new batch.

events.title: The board is not straight
events.text: A board prepared for a carved fitting has bent while drying. Cutting the planned shape now would leave a poor fit.

choices.text: Mark a smaller fitting that will fit the wood

outcomes.text: You change the layout and cut the smaller fitting. The customer needs fewer pieces than planned, but the fit is sound.

choices.text: Buy a replacement board for 5 drachmas

outcomes.text: You spend 5 drachmas on another board and keep the original measurements.

choices.text: Set it aside and explain the delay

outcomes.text: You explain why the board cannot be used as planned. The customer agrees to wait while you find suitable material.

events.title: A flaw in the stone
events.text: A dark line appears as you cut a small stone relief. You cannot yet tell whether it is only on the surface.

choices.text: Stop and check the line with another worker

outcomes.text: You check the surface together and alter the shallow cut. The flaw stays outside the main detail.

choices.text: Simplify the design around the flaw

outcomes.text: You redraw the border and explain the change to the customer before cutting farther.

choices.text: Set the piece aside for a later job

outcomes.text: You put the flawed piece aside and tell the customer you need another stone. The job remains unfinished.

events.title: A gap in the original
events.text: The text you are copying has an unreadable word. Guessing would make the finished copy look complete, but might change its meaning.

choices.text: Mark the gap clearly

outcomes.text: You leave a clear mark for the missing word. The recipient knows exactly where the original was unreadable.

choices.text: Ask to compare another copy

outcomes.text: Another copy preserves the missing word. You check it carefully and finish the line.

choices.text: Ask the owner how they want the gap handled

outcomes.text: You show the damaged line to the owner and agree how to mark it in the finished copy.

events.title: A learner disagrees
events.text: A learner challenges the example you used in a discussion. They can explain why it does not fit their experience.

choices.text: Work through their objection

outcomes.text: You ask them to explain each step, then revise the example together. The discussion lasts longer than the lesson you planned.

choices.text: Ask the group to compare two examples

outcomes.text: The learners compare the examples and identify where each one breaks down.

choices.text: Leave the question for the next lesson

outcomes.text: You write down the objection and return to the remaining material. You will need a better example next time.

events.title: Cloud hides the observation
events.text: Cloud covers the part of the sky you planned to observe. There is still an earlier table to check indoors.

choices.text: Check the arithmetic in the earlier table

outcomes.text: You compare the entries and recalculate a short section. One copied number needs correction.

choices.text: Record that the observation was not made

outcomes.text: You mark the missed observation clearly rather than entering an estimate as if you had seen it.

choices.text: Put the work away for the night

outcomes.text: You cover the working sheet and leave the observation for another clear night.

events.title: A rope is too short
events.text: A rope prepared for a shore task does not reach the intended fastening. The crew asks how to rearrange the work.

choices.text: Move the load before fastening it

outcomes.text: The crew shifts the load to a position the rope can reach. You check the new arrangement before the work continues.

choices.text: Find a suitable replacement rope

outcomes.text: You fetch another rope and check its length before bringing it back. The task starts later, with the planned arrangement.

choices.text: Wait for the experienced crew to decide

outcomes.text: You keep the area clear while the experienced crew changes the arrangement.

events.title: A younger worker asks for advice
events.text: A younger worker asks how you handled a routine problem. You have time to show them, talk it through or leave it for another day.

choices.text: Demonstrate the task slowly

outcomes.text: You show each step and let the younger worker repeat it. They get the last part right without another prompt.

choices.text: Explain how to check their own work

outcomes.text: You point out the signs of a mistake and ask them to inspect their attempt. The correction is theirs to make.

choices.text: Suggest asking again on a quieter day

outcomes.text: You explain that you cannot give the task enough attention today. They agree to return another time.

events.title: Things kept for years
events.text: You are sorting household possessions and find several small tools nobody has used for years.

choices.text: Pass a few on to someone who can use them

outcomes.text: You give the unused tools to someone who needs them and keep the ones still useful at home.

choices.text: Explain each tool and sort them by use

outcomes.text: You show the household what each tool does. The useful pieces are put where someone can find them.

choices.text: Wrap them and put them back

outcomes.text: You wrap the tools to keep them dry and put them back in storage. There is more room after the rest is sorted.

events.title: Held for ransom
events.text: Two armed men force you into a yard beside the street. They demand 30 drachmas to let you leave. You can still hear people passing in the lane.

choices.text: Pay 30 drachmas to be released

outcomes.text: You hand over 30 drachmas. The men open the gate, and you leave the yard without an injury.

choices.text: Shout for help from the lane

outcomes.text: People gather outside the yard. The men release you and leave by another passage before the crowd comes in.

weightModifiers.reason: People nearby recognize your voice

outcomes.text: A man strikes you as you shout. The noise brings people to the entrance, and the men flee before they can take you farther.

opportunity.label: Help arrives before you are hurt

choices.text: Talk them into letting you go

outcomes.text: You keep talking until the men decide holding you is more trouble than it is worth. They let you walk back into the lane.

weightModifiers.reason: You can keep the conversation under control
You can name people nearby who will look for you

outcomes.text: They shove you against the wall and strike you before letting you leave. You reach home bruised.
One man strikes your lower leg as you try to move past him. You leave with an open tibial fracture and need care.

choices.text: Force past them and run

outcomes.text: You push through the gap and reach the busy lane. The men stop chasing when other people turn to watch.

weightModifiers.reason: You can move quickly

outcomes.text: You get through the gate, but a blow to your lower leg knocks you down. People drive the men away. You have an open tibial fracture and need care.
One of the men stabs you in the chest as you force past him. The wound proves fatal.

events.title: Mistaken for a cargo thief
events.text: A guard stops you near a cargo yard. Someone has described a thief wearing clothes like yours, and the guard wants to hold you while the missing bundle is found.

choices.text: Stay and give a clear account of your errand

outcomes.text: You explain where you have been and wait beside the gate. The missing bundle is found in another store, and the guard lets you leave.

choices.text: Ask them to bring someone who knows you

outcomes.text: A worker recognizes you and confirms your errand. You are released before the yard closes.

weightModifiers.reason: You have people nearby who will speak for you

outcomes.text: Nobody who can confirm your story arrives in time. You wait until the bundle is found, then leave hungry and tired.

choices.text: Ask them to check the cargo marks again

outcomes.text: You point out that two bundles carry similar marks. The guard has both checked and finds the missing goods without taking you farther.

events.title: A purse under the bench
events.text: You find a small purse under a public bench. It contains coins and a marked token. A trader nearby is searching the ground, but has not noticed you.

choices.text: Hand the purse to the searching trader

outcomes.text: The trader describes the token before you show it. You return the purse, and they thank you before hurrying away.

choices.text: Ask about the token before returning it

outcomes.text: The trader correctly describes the token and names the place where the purse was lost. They give you 10 drachmas after you return it.
The trader describes the purse correctly. You return it, but there is no reward beyond their thanks.

choices.text: Keep the coins and leave the purse

outcomes.text: You take 20 drachmas and leave the empty purse under the bench. The trader continues searching while you walk away.
The trader sees you taking the coins. People nearby make you return them, and the argument follows you into the street.

events.title: A visitor offers a commission
events.text: A visitor sees a piece of your work and asks for a small sample for their household. They offer 20 drachmas for a finished piece they can use.

choices.text: Turn down the extra work

outcomes.text: You explain that you cannot take the commission. The visitor asks another worker.

choices.text: Prepare a clean copy for 20 drachmas

outcomes.text: You prepare the requested copy and check it before delivery. The visitor accepts it and pays 20 drachmas.

choices.text: Make a wooden fitting for 20 drachmas

outcomes.text: You measure and make the small fitting, then adjust it at the visitor's home. They pay 20 drachmas when it fits.

choices.text: Finish a clay vessel for 20 drachmas

outcomes.text: You make and finish a small clay vessel with the agreed decoration. The visitor collects it after firing and pays 20 drachmas.

events.title: A beam cracks above the lane
events.text: A beam cracks above a narrow lane. A worker slips against a hanging rope while the people underneath begin to move away.

choices.text: Move clear of the falling timber

outcomes.text: You step away and keep others from entering the lane. Workers deal with the damaged frame before the passage opens again.

choices.text: Warn the people coming around the corner

outcomes.text: You shout until the approaching carriers stop. Everyone stays clear while other workers lower the damaged timber.

choices.text: Help pull the worker clear

outcomes.text: You and another person pull the worker clear before the timber falls. Your arms shake after the effort, but both of you can walk away.

weightModifiers.reason: You have the strength for the pull
You recognize which fastening is still holding

outcomes.text: The worker gets clear, but falling timber strikes your lower leg. You suffer an open tibial fracture and need care.

opportunity.label: Get the worker clear without an injury

events.title: A crewmate falls overboard
events.text: A crewmate loses their footing and falls into the water. They surface near the ship, but cannot reach the side. A loose rope lies on the deck.

choices.text: Throw the rope and call the crew

outcomes.text: You throw the rope within reach and call for help. The crew hauls the crewmate alongside and gets them back aboard.

choices.text: Secure the rope and help haul them aboard

outcomes.text: You secure the rope and work with the crew to bring the crewmate aboard. The pull leaves you sore, but you finish the job.

choices.text: Jump into the water after them

outcomes.text: You reach the crewmate and help them hold the rope. The crew pulls you both alongside before you lose your grip.

weightModifiers.reason: You know how to use the ship's lines in the water
You have enough strength for the effort

outcomes.text: The current pulls you away from the crewmate. The crew gets a second rope to you and brings you aboard exhausted. Another sailor reaches your crewmate.
You lose your grip before the crew can reach you. You are pulled under and drown during the rescue.

events.title: A demanding workshop review
events.text: Experienced makers examine the methods behind your recent work. They ask you to explain a difficult part of the method, then compare your answer with the work in front of them.

choices.text: Make the workshop's finest clay vessel

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already highly developed
You use these techniques in your regular work
You can plan and check the difficult parts

outcomes.text: The vessel is accepted, but a small flaw remains in the rim. You practise correcting that part before the next firing.

choices.text: Carve a matching set of wooden fittings

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already highly developed
You use these techniques in your regular work
You can plan and check the difficult parts

outcomes.text: You finish the fittings, then rework two that sit unevenly. The corrections give you more practice.

choices.text: Finish a demanding stone relief

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already highly developed
You use these techniques in your regular work
You can plan and check the difficult parts

outcomes.text: You finish the relief, but simplify a detail you cannot cut cleanly. Another worker helps you practise that cut on scrap stone.

choices.text: Build and fit a precise wooden assembly

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already highly developed
You use these techniques in your regular work
You can plan and check the difficult parts

outcomes.text: The assembly works after several adjustments. You identify which measurements caused the extra work.

choices.text: Leave the commission to another worker

outcomes.text: You decline the commission and continue your own work.

events.title: An exacting scholarly review
events.text: Readers ask you to defend a difficult step in your explanation. They point out where an assumption needs defending and where a comparison would strengthen the account.

choices.text: Prepare an exact copy of a difficult text

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your subject knowledge is already advanced
You can connect the details of the work
You practise this subject in your regular work

outcomes.text: Your copy is useful, but the reader finds passages that need another comparison. You work through them together.

choices.text: Defend an argument before the readers

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your subject knowledge is already advanced
You can connect the details of the work
You practise this subject in your regular work

outcomes.text: One objection exposes a weak step. You revise the argument after the discussion and test it against another example.

choices.text: Recalculate and check a difficult sky table

outcomes.text: You recalculate the table, explain the method and catch every copied error in the final check. Astronomy reaches its cap.

weightModifiers.reason: Your subject knowledge is already advanced
You can connect the details of the work
You practise this subject in your regular work

outcomes.text: The reader finds a mismatch in one column. You trace it to an earlier calculation and work it through again.

choices.text: Explain the methods in several traditional charts

outcomes.text: You reconstruct the chart methods and explain where the traditional readings disagree. Astrology reaches its cap; the exercise establishes no prediction about the future.

weightModifiers.reason: Your subject knowledge is already advanced
You can connect the details of the work
You practise this subject in your regular work

outcomes.text: One chart uses a convention you do not recognize. You compare examples with the reader before finishing your explanation.

choices.text: Keep the work private for now

outcomes.text: You turn down the demonstration and continue studying on your own.

events.title: The missing part of the method
events.text: A reader shares a difficult collection of worked examples. You recognize most of the methods, and a connection between them may resolve questions you have studied for years.

choices.text: Work through the examples and explain the connection

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: Your existing knowledge covers most of the problem
You can compare the difficult passages directly
You can verify the calculations yourself

outcomes.text: You resolve some of the questions, but the general method still needs work. The reader leaves you another example to check.

choices.text: Leave the examples for another time

outcomes.text: You put the examples aside and return to your ordinary tasks.

events.title: The neighborhood puts its trust in you
events.text: Several households ask you to settle a shared supply agreement. They know your past work, but each has different needs. Getting everyone to accept one arrangement would strengthen your standing across the neighborhood.

choices.text: Hear each household and arrange a shared agreement

outcomes.text: Experienced practitioners review your methods and give specific feedback. You leave with a clearer method and a practical question to carry into your next work year.

weightModifiers.reason: You can keep the discussion clear and practical
The households already place great trust in you
You can check how the different terms fit together

outcomes.text: Most households accept the terms, but two keep separate arrangements. You settle the immediate dispute and agree which details still need discussion.

choices.text: Ask the households to choose another representative

outcomes.text: You explain that you cannot take on the agreement. The households find another person to arrange it.

events.title: The song you ask for
events.text: You recognize a familiar song before the singer reaches the second line. You protest whenever they try a different one.

events.title: A knot in a cloth
events.text: A relative ties a knot in the corner of a cloth and lets you pull it loose. You bring the cloth back each time it comes undone.

events.title: A bright patch on the floor
events.text: Light falls through a gap above the doorway. You put your hand into the bright patch and watch the shadow move.

events.title: A visitor holds out their hands
events.text: A visitor offers to pick you up. You stay with your usual carer until the visitor stops reaching and starts making faces instead.

events.title: The door has a new color
events.text: You stop outside the wrong doorway after a neighbor repaints their door. A familiar adult calls you back before you go inside.

events.title: A knot below your knee
events.text: You keep stopping to inspect a loose fastening on your clothes. An adult reties it and asks you to leave it alone until you get home.

events.title: A row that keeps changing
events.text: You arrange large stones beside the doorway. People stepping past disturb the row, and you spend the afternoon putting it back.

events.title: Waiting for your turn
events.text: Another child keeps a toy longer than agreed. An adult helps you count a short wait before the toy changes hands.

events.title: An order you remember
events.text: You remember the items on a small household errand without being prompted. The adult with you still checks them before paying.

events.title: The shortcut is shut
events.text: A passage you use for errands is blocked by stored goods. You return by a longer route and explain why the trip took more time.

events.title: An offcut put to use
events.text: You bring home a small wooden offcut with permission. An adult helps you smooth its edge and use it under a rocking stool.

events.title: One more than expected
events.text: You count a group of empty containers twice and get different answers. One was hidden behind a hanging cloth.

events.title: A parcel above the shop
events.text: You watch a relative wrap a small purchase for a customer. They let you hold the loose end of the cord while the knot is tied.

events.title: A mark in spare clay
events.text: Your relatives set aside a little spare clay while preparing an order. You press a pattern into it and leave it on the edge of the bench.

events.title: Rope at the doorway
events.text: A relative brings home a length of worn packing rope. You help spread it out while they decide which pieces can still be used.

events.title: A float to check
events.text: Your household sorts equipment after a fishing trip. A relative shows you how an intact float sits in a shallow bowl of water.

events.title: Flour on your clothes
events.text: A relative finds flour on the front of your clothes after you have watched dough being prepared. You help shake it off away from the working bench.

events.title: The blank side of a sheet
events.text: Someone in your household turns over a used work sheet and lets you draw on the blank part. They put the important documents farther back on the shelf.

events.title: A short length of thread
events.text: A relative gives you a short piece of spare thread while they wind a working bundle. You keep comparing its color with the thread still on the bench.

events.title: A word from the old village
events.text: A visiting relative uses a word your household knows from the Delta. You repeat it until someone explains what it means in the neighborhood.

events.title: The faces in the procession
events.text: Philista lays out a design with one figure behind another: a procession, crowded into a shallow strip of stone. Menon taps the place where two faces meet. Can you separate them without cutting too deep?

choices.text: Carve the procession relief

outcomes.text: Menon turns {name}'s Procession Relief toward the light. The faces remain distinct even in the shallowest cuts; Philista accepts the work and pays you. Other makers ask to look before the piece leaves the bench.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: Menon turns the relief sideways, and two faces disappear into the same ridge. Philista asks you to rework that section. You keep the earlier commission to your name and return to the difficult cuts.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: A visitor asks who made the figure
events.text: A neighbour has seen {work:sculpture-first-work} in Philista's room and wants something for their own shelf. Menon brings them to your bench. You agree a smaller paid order before they leave.

events.title: The figure comes back for a repair
events.text: Philista still keeps {work:sculpture-first-work}, though an edge now needs attention. Menon brings a younger worker to watch you repair it. You are paid to check a second piece while the tools are out.

events.title: The objection in the margin
events.text: Kleio returns your discussion notes with a question beside the final argument. Apollonios has marked a different difficulty on the same sheet. They offer to gather a regular circle if you can make the reasoning hold.

choices.text: Revise the discussions and defend the argument

outcomes.text: Kleio follows the revised argument in {name}'s Collected Discussions, then tries a new objection. This time you can answer it without changing your starting claim. Apollonios arranges the next meeting and pays for the completed work.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: Kleio finds a case your rule does not cover. Apollonios waits while you try the argument again, but the difficulty remains. You take the notes home to revise; the earlier lesson remains yours.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: Your pupil brings a pupil
events.text: Kleio arrives with someone she now teaches and a copy of {work:philosophy-first-work}. They disagree about the second example. Apollonios pays you to check their copy before the next discussion.

events.title: A rule brought to the dinner table
events.text: Apollonios has tried the argument in {work:philosophy-first-work} on a household disagreement. Kleio brings both versions of the quarrel. You revise an example with them and receive payment for another lesson.

events.title: A passage that needs a steady hand
events.text: Nikeratos spreads out the load list and leaves a space for your plan. The passage will need more careful preparation than your last delivery; Tasos wants the crew and every entrusted package accounted for at the other end.

choices.text: Plan and undertake the difficult passage

outcomes.text: The last package comes ashore with its binding intact. Tasos checks it off against {name}'s Safe Return while Nikeratos counts the crew. They pay you and recommend you for more responsibility aboard.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: Nikeratos finds a weak point in your plan before it can be accepted. Tasos asks you to work through the load list again. Your earlier delivery stands, but this passage needs more preparation.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: A crew asks for you by name
events.text: Another crew asks Nikeratos who they should trust with a delivery. He names you and cites {work:seafaring-first-work}. Tasos pays you to help prepare the next cargo.

events.title: The old receipt settles the count
events.text: Tasos returns with a disputed quantity and the receipt from {work:seafaring-first-work}. Nikeratos remembers the loading. Together you settle the count, and the customer pays you to check another delivery.

events.title: An assignment with no room for confusion
events.text: Dion brings an awkward assignment: several tasks must be done in order, with stores accounted for at every handover. Herakleides asks you to explain who will do what. A clear plan could earn a commendation, though neither man offers you a new rank.

choices.text: Organise the unit assignment

outcomes.text: Dion checks the completed assignment against your plan. Herakleides enters {name}'s Unit Commendation, recording how the stores and duties were handled. You receive the payment; a new rank still requires a separate appointment.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: Dion stops at a handover your plan has left unclear. Herakleides asks you to rehearse that part with the others before it can be accepted. Your previous service remains on record.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: Pay still owed for old service
events.text: Herakleides uncovers an unsettled service account. Dion checks it against {work:military-first-work}, and the outstanding payment reaches you. The old record settles the debt without creating a new appointment.

events.title: Stores to check in a different household
events.text: A household needs someone to check its stores, and Herakleides gives them your name. Dion points to {work:military-first-work} as evidence that you can keep an account. You are paid for the civilian work, under whichever government now rules the neighborhood.

events.title: A customer wants the next order too
events.text: Berenike lays your last receipt beside a list of goods needed again. Sarapion is willing to supply them, if the accounts and responsibilities are agreed first. They ask whether you can turn one completed order into a continuing arrangement.

choices.text: Negotiate the repeat supply agreement

outcomes.text: Sarapion checks the supplier's entries; Berenike checks what will arrive and when. Both accept the arrangement. Orders carrying {name}'s Trading Seal now identify your shared venture, and you receive the agreed payment.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: Sarapion and Berenike cannot agree on an entry your plan leaves unsettled. The continuing arrangement must wait. You keep the earlier completed order and go back through the account.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: The customer brings the receipt back
events.text: Berenike puts {work:commerce-first-work} on the table and asks for another order. Sarapion remembers being paid on time. You arrange a smaller batch within your means and receive payment for the work.

events.title: A disputed line in the old account
events.text: Sarapion questions a line in {work:commerce-first-work}. Berenike still has the receipt that explains it. Once the figures agree, another household pays you to check its own account.

events.title: The column that will not agree
events.text: Heron and Isidora lay several table copies side by side. One column disagrees with the others, and the error has travelled into a second copy. They ask you to prepare a checked collection with a clear account of the corrections.

choices.text: Compare the tables and explain the corrections

outcomes.text: Heron follows the arithmetic in {name}'s Compared Tables without finding the old error. Isidora marks the corrections as yours and accepts the collection. Your notes distinguish calculations from seasonal expectations that may still prove wrong.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: Heron reaches a total that still disagrees with your copy. Isidora sets the two sheets beside each other so you can trace the difference. The earlier corrected table keeps its credit; this collection is not ready yet.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: A fresh copy of the table
events.text: Isidora has worn her copy of {work:astronomy-calendar-first-work} thin at the folds. Heron checks a corrected column with you while you prepare another. The household pays for the fresh copy.

events.title: An error in someone else's copy
events.text: Heron brings a version of {work:astronomy-calendar-first-work} with a total you do not recognise. Isidora traces the copied error back to one line. You are paid for a corrected version, with the method still credited to you.

events.title: The entrance everyone must catch
events.text: Melitta brings a programme that needs several performers to enter together. Theon wants the ensemble for another gathering, but first asks to hear how you will hold the difficult passage together. The invitation depends on the rehearsal.

choices.text: Lead the ensemble through the programme

outcomes.text: Melitta catches your signal, and the others enter with her. {name}'s Ensemble Repertoire reaches its final phrase without the passage breaking apart. Theon pays you and commissions another engagement, crediting you for bringing the performers together.

weightModifiers.reason: Your developed technique supports the undertaking
A remembered early interest supports your preparation for this opportunity.

outcomes.text: One entrance comes too soon and carries the others with it. Melitta stops the rehearsal so you can work on the cue. Theon's invitation must wait; your earlier paid engagement remains on record.

choices.text: Keep to your current work

outcomes.text: You keep to the work you have already agreed.

events.title: The host requests a familiar piece
events.text: Theon asks for a piece from {work:music-performance-first-work} at another gathering. Melitta remembers where the entrances once went astray. You rehearse them together and are paid for the repeat engagement.

events.title: A performer arrives knowing your programme
events.text: Melitta brings a new performer who heard about {work:music-performance-first-work} at Theon's house. You work through the entrances until the group can follow the same cue. The rehearsal earns you a further payment.

events.title: A quay receipt and a household order
events.text: Nikeratos lays down the quay receipt; Berenike brings the household's order. Comparing {work:seafaring-first-work} with {work:commerce-first-work} settles the disputed delivery. You are paid for the extra account work.

events.title: The performers need a passage
events.text: Melitta has an engagement to reach and performers to get aboard. Nikeratos recalls {work:seafaring-first-work}; you bring out the plan for {work:music-performance-first-work}. Between you, the passage and the performers' needs are settled, and the planning is paid.

events.title: An animal without ears
events.text: Your carer sets a lump of clay before you. One person calls it a goat; another insists it is a dog. At present it has neither ears nor a tail to settle the matter.

choices.text: Press ears and a tail into the clay

outcomes.text: Your carer steadies the lump while you press on the ears and tail. Now you want another piece, for a second animal.

choices.text: Ask why the others see different animals

outcomes.text: You point at the same lump and ask each person again. Their answers change, and you want to know why.

choices.text: Go and play with something else

outcomes.text: You leave the clay on the mat and turn to another game. Its identity remains unsettled.

events.title: An answer on the bowl
events.text: The meal is too hot to eat. While you wait, someone taps a little pattern on an empty wooden bowl, then pauses and looks at you.

choices.text: Tap the rhythm back

outcomes.text: You tap back, miss a beat and try again. The other person answers with a new pattern, and supper has to wait another moment.

choices.text: Count the taps with your fingers

outcomes.text: You hold up a finger for each tap. An extra sound catches you short, and your carer helps you begin the count again.

choices.text: Wait for the food instead

outcomes.text: You leave the bowl quiet and watch the steam rising from your meal.

events.title: Sunlight on the floor
events.text: A bright patch lies across the floor. Each time you come back, it has slipped a little farther towards the wall. Your carer stops to see what you are watching.

choices.text: Put a pebble at its edge

outcomes.text: You set a pebble at the edge, with your carer keeping it clear of the doorway. When you return, the light has left it behind.

choices.text: Invent a voice for the moving patch

outcomes.text: You give the patch a voice. Your carer answers, and for a while the room contains a conversation with the sunlight.

choices.text: Find another game

outcomes.text: You leave the light to cross the room without you and go to another game.

events.title: The bundle that opens again
events.text: A folded cloth keeps falling open as the household puts things away. Your carer takes a short piece of spare cord and makes a loose loop. You reach to see how it holds.

choices.text: Try making the loose loop

outcomes.text: Your carer watches your hands while you work the short cord. At last the loop stays together when you pull.

choices.text: Arrange the corners into a shape

outcomes.text: You press the cloth's corners into a new outline. The shape pleases you more than the knot, and you begin folding another scrap.

choices.text: Let your carer finish

outcomes.text: You give back the cord. Your carer ties the cloth and puts it away.

events.title: Whose turn comes first?
events.text: The children have laid scraps into a path across the courtyard. Two of them step onto the first piece at once. The game stops while everyone claims the next turn.

choices.text: Help agree a turn for everyone

outcomes.text: With a carer's help, you name who follows whom. Feet begin moving along the path again.

choices.text: Ask why one child should go first

outcomes.text: You ask why that child should go first. The others offer reasons, and you go on asking even after the game has changed.

choices.text: Go to another game

outcomes.text: You step away from the path. Behind you, the argument about turns continues.

events.title: A reed on the water
events.text: Your carer sets a shallow washing bowl within reach. A short reed stays on the surface; a little stone drops to the bottom. You point from one to the other.

choices.text: Try balancing a scrap on the reed

outcomes.text: Your carer holds the bowl while you balance light scraps on the reed. One tips into the water, and you ask to try another.

choices.text: Keep comparing the reed and stone

outcomes.text: You put the reed and stone in again and again. Your carer answers your questions, then has to think harder when you repeat them.

choices.text: Leave the bowl with your carer

outcomes.text: You dry your hands and go to something else. Your carer lifts the stone out of the water.

events.title: The fuller-looking cup
events.text: Your carer divides a snack between two cups. One is tall and narrow, the other low and broad. Someone is certain the tall cup has more.

choices.text: Count the pieces in each cup

outcomes.text: You match the pieces one by one, with help. When the last pair is counted, the portions seem different from how they first looked.

choices.text: Ask what makes the division fair

outcomes.text: You ask why the division is fair. The adults begin with the pieces, move on to the cups, and are still talking when the snack is gone.

choices.text: Eat your share

outcomes.text: You eat without settling the question. Soon both cups are empty.

events.title: Who is behind the cloth?
events.text: A cloth puppet appears above a hanging sheet and begins asking questions. You know the older child hiding behind it, but the voice makes you laugh. Your carer sits nearby.

choices.text: Give a second puppet a different voice
