influences.label: Alexander levies the city: people of military age must serve, flee or pay.

event.title: A levy in the king's name
event.text: Officers acting for Alexander are filling garrison and supply posts in Egypt. Your name is on the district list of people fit to serve. The recruiting officer will accept a substitute's fee, and some on the list have already left for relatives in the Delta.

choices.text: Answer the levy and report for service

outcomes.text: You serve a season in a coastal garrison and learn drill under a Macedonian officer. The pay is small and the days are long. When your term ends you return to your household.
Your file leader notices that you keep the others in step and the supply tallies honest. He sends your name to an officer with his report before your term ends.

weightModifiers.reason: You already know basic drill
You can keep a supply tally

outcomes.text: A fall on a supply march leaves you lame. You finish your term in the stores and carry the injury home.

weightModifiers.reason: Good health carries you through the marches

choices.text: Leave for relatives in the Delta until the officers move on

outcomes.text: You spend the season in a relative's village, working for your keep. When you come back the officers have moved on, but your neighbours remember that you were gone.

weightModifiers.reason: Relatives are willing to hide you
You can find passage on a river boat

outcomes.text: Officers are checking the boats at the canal. You are brought back, fined and made to serve a season in the garrison after all.

choices.text: Pay the 60-drachma substitute fee

outcomes.text: The officer takes the fee and enters a hired man in your place. Your household keeps its work, and your name comes off the roll.

influences.label: Alexander founds and builds: new work and building plots open in the city.

event.title: Work on the new city
event.text: Surveyors have marked the streets of Alexander's new city beside Rhakotis. Contractors are hiring for walls, quays and houses, and plots along the new streets are being let to anyone who can pay toward the building.

choices.text: Take paid work on the building sites

outcomes.text: You carry stone, mix mortar and learn how the builders set a line. The pay is steady while the work lasts.
A foreman sees that you can keep count and puts you in charge of a work gang's tallies. You finish the season with better pay and a name the contractors know.

weightModifiers.reason: You can keep a work tally

choices.text: Put 40 drachmas toward a share in a building plot

outcomes.text: The street fills faster than the surveyors expected. Your share is let to newcomers, and the rent comes in before the year is out.

weightModifiers.reason: You can judge the contractor's accounts

outcomes.text: Building stalls when the contractor is called away to the harbour works. You sell the share and recover part of your money.

choices.text: Keep to your own work

outcomes.text: You keep to your existing work and watch the new streets fill from a distance.

influences.label: Aristotle founds the Lyceum: young people study notes from his lectures.

event.title: Notes from the Lyceum
event.text: A reader back from Athens has copied notes from Aristotle's lectures at the Lyceum: what things are made of, why they change and how to argue about them. He offers to go through them with any young person who can keep up.

choices.text: Work through the notes with him

outcomes.text: Week after week you test the questions against things you can see: a seed, a tide, a broken pot. You begin to ask why as readily as what.

weightModifiers.reason: You can already read the notes yourself

outcomes.text: Most of the notes are beyond you this year, but the reader leaves you one question to keep: what makes a thing what it is.

choices.text: Keep to your household work

outcomes.text: You thank the reader and keep to your work. Others in the street borrow the notes.

influences.label: Aristotle tutors the court: royal children learn argument and composure.

event.title: A tutor for the royal household
event.text: Your family has engaged a tutor trained in Aristotle's school, as Philip of Macedon once engaged Aristotle for his son. The lessons cover reading, argument, the conduct of rulers and keeping a clear head when others lose theirs.

choices.text: Attend the lessons and argue back

outcomes.text: The tutor makes you defend every claim and answer calmly when pressed. As an exercise he has you check the household guard's supply lists, then writes to their officer commending your work.

choices.text: Spend the hours riding and hunting instead

outcomes.text: You keep to the stables and the hunting grounds. The tutor teaches your cousins, though some of his questions reach you at meals.

influences.label: Euclid opens a school: children learn letters and figures.

event.title: A school of demonstrations
event.text: A teacher following Euclid's method has opened a school near the harbour. Children draw figures in sand trays and must say why each step follows from the last. The fee is small, and some pupils pay in errands.

choices.text: Go to the lessons

outcomes.text: You learn letters from the written propositions and numbers from the figures. By the end of the year you can prove a small thing and say why it holds.

choices.text: Run errands for the school and listen at the door

outcomes.text: You carry water and messages for the teacher and pick up what you can between errands.

influences.label: Euclid keeps to the Museum: gifted readers may be offered a scholar's post.

event.title: A place among the Museum's scholars
event.text: Scholars working beside Euclid at the Museum need a capable reader to check figures and copy proofs. The post carries a stipend and use of the collected books, but the work is exacting and careless help is soon dismissed.

choices.text: Accept the post and work through the proofs

outcomes.text: You check constructions line by line and copy the corrected proofs. At the end of the season the scholars keep your name among those they recommend for paid work.

weightModifiers.reason: Your reckoning is already strong

outcomes.text: An error in your first copied figure costs you the scholars' trust, and the post goes to another reader. You keep what you learned checking their work.

choices.text: Decline and keep your present work

outcomes.text: You decline the post. The scholars find another reader, and your own work goes on as before.

influences.label: Cleomenes corners the grain: merchants profit while poor households go short.

event.title: Grain held for the export price
event.text: Cleomenes, who manages Egypt's revenues for the king, has bought up the district's grain to sell to famine-struck Greek cities at a high price. Bread in the market now costs twice what it did. Merchants with silver are buying shares in the cargoes; everyone else must pay or go short.

choices.text: Put 40 drachmas into a share of an export cargo

outcomes.text: The cargo sells in a hungry Greek port at the price Cleomenes set. Your share comes back nearly doubled, though your neighbours know where the profit came from.

weightModifiers.reason: You can check the cargo accounts
You already work in the trade

outcomes.text: The ship is held at the harbour while officials argue over the export duty. When the share is finally settled, you recover only part of your money.

choices.text: Pay the high price to keep the household fed

outcomes.text: You pay what the sellers ask. The household eats as before, but your savings are thinner by the end of the season.

choices.text: Eat less until the price falls

outcomes.text: Meals shrink to bread and a little oil. The household gets through the season weaker and short-tempered.
Neighbours pool what they have and share it out. The season is lean, but nobody in the street goes entirely without bread.

weightModifiers.reason: Neighbours share with people they trust

influences.label: Cleomenes fills the granaries: rations reach households weakened in the famine years.

event.title: The granaries open
event.text: The grain shortage that has struck the Greek cities reaches your district, and you are already weak. Officials open the royal granaries that Cleomenes had filled and issue measured rations. Clerks write each household's name against its share.

influences.label: A teacher took you in hand for a season and drilled your letters.
A reader lent you a book roll and talked it over with you.
A veteran took you under his wing and taught you to keep your footing.
A soldier warned you that the recruiters were coming, so you put food and silver aside.
A merchant extended you credit on easy terms when you needed it.
A trader hired you for a season of paid work at the quays.
A workshop master took you on and taught you the trade's first skills.
A craftsman shared part of a paid commission with you.
An interpreter of the sky read a favourable omen for you.
A sky-watcher warned of a hard year, and your household stored food against it.
A musician's playing lifted your spirits through a hard week.
A troupe of performers lent your household a hand when it was struggling.

rules.title: Fieldwork
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 annual fieldwork action, hired or on a household plot.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock ordinary cultivation plan; +3 Farming from each subsequent completed farming work year.

rules.title: Seed handling
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 sowing cycle with its seed debited from inventory; retain seed for the following cycle.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock a seed reserve: default 10 grain per grain plot, protected from automatic surplus sales. Flax sowing consumes 2 purchased flax-seed units/plot; reserve that input separately.

rules.title: Soil knowledge
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 soil-preparation work year; record plot allocation and resulting harvest.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock soil preparation: spend the annual work action for +5% gross grain/flax yield this year; no automatic bonus.

rules.title: Water management
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 channel-maintenance work year, including its quoted cost; no low flood required.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock maintained channels: 8 dr per plot/year; low-flood yield factor becomes 0.55 instead of 0.45 while maintained; other flood factors unchanged.

rules.title: Seasonal planning
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 planned harvest with recorded plot/labour allocation and seed reserve.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock annual production-plan preview with rent, rations, seed, feed and remaining saleable surplus; unlock both specializations.

rules.title: Sowing methods
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 prepared sowing cycle with full seed allocation.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock dense sowing: consume 20 rather than 10 seed grain per plot; +6% gross yield at normal/high flood, no yield increase at low flood.

rules.title: Crop care
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 crop-care work years.
rules.rewardDescription: Crop-care activity gives +8% gross yield in its work year instead of the +5% soil-preparation action; they are alternative annual actions.

rules.title: Water allocation
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 maintained-channel harvests, under any flood condition.
rules.rewardDescription: Maintained-channel low-flood factor becomes 0.60; maintenance remains 8 dr/plot/year; replaces the 0.55 effect.

rules.title: Crop allocation
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 different single-crop harvest plans (grain then flax, or the reverse), retaining the applicable next-year seed. Mixed allocation is not required before its unlock.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock coordinated mixed-crop planning; +5% flax yield on assigned flax plots; grain plots and animal feed remain actual resource constraints.

rules.title: Yield reliability
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 planned harvests whose household grain ledger reconciles, with full household rations.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock conservative planting: +15% gross yield during low flood, -5% at normal/high flood; alternative to dense sowing, never stacked with it.

rules.title: Integrated cultivation
rules.proofDescription: Complete a 2-work-year integrated plan, each year providing full household rations and next-year seed.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock one integrated annual action combining channel maintenance with crop care within available labour; pay both costs. Combined sowing/crop-care/flax plan bonuses are capped at +20%; flood-factor correction is separate. Qualify for master cultivator work offers.

rules.title: Grain preservation
rules.proofDescription: Store at least 240 grain across 1 annual settlement; the household must receive full rations.
rules.rewardDescription: Reduce the configured in-capacity grain spoilage rate by 15% relative: 8% becomes 6.8%; never changes over-capacity spoilage. Apply after existing reductions; total in-capacity reduction cannot exceed 75% of configured base.

rules.title: Reserve budgeting
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 settlement retaining a full coming-year household ration plus seed; food served must be recorded.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock protected food/seed reserve plans. Voluntary sales below reserve require an explicit override; reserves create no grain.

rules.title: Storehouse management
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 paid store repair/inspection and 1 annual stock reconciliation.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock a +500-capacity store extension: 80 dr, 4 timber and 5 clay, 1 work year; upkeep 4 dr/year. Materials and paid work are separate recorded costs; one extension per household.

rules.title: Reserve replenishment
rules.proofDescription: Restore the full food/seed reserve in 2 different years after normal household consumption.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock automatic surplus allocation targets: food, seed, animal feed, then sale. Reduce in-capacity spoilage by 25% relative to base, replacing the earlier 15%.

rules.title: Shortage preparedness
rules.proofDescription: Either feed the household fully during 1 low-flood year using reserves, OR finish 2 years with stored food covering 1.5 annual household rations plus seed.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock contingency purchase plans capped by player cash and merchant stock; never borrow automatically. Spoilage reduction becomes 30% relative to base, replacing 25%.

rules.title: Resilient husbandry
rules.proofDescription: Complete 3 consecutive annual settlements with full rations, seed reserved and no new emergency food debt; the same years may be ordinary flood years.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock a 2-year reserve/maintenance plan using existing resources; in-capacity spoilage reduction becomes 35% relative to base, replacing 30%. Qualify for master household-farmer work offers.

rules.title: Safe hand tools
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 supervised tool-practice work year; workshop-owned practice stock is not player inventory.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock hired workshop practice and rental tools; introductory access fee 2 dr per work year.

rules.title: Measuring and cutting
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 measurement/cutting exercise within 5% of the stated exercise target dimensions.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock measured material estimates for recipes and cutting exercises; no material-efficiency discount yet.

rules.title: Material preparation
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 preparation jobs in any one of textiles, clay or wood/stone. Distinct work years; each job records paid inputs.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock supervised starter templates for thread, linen, one basic garment, one fired vessel or one clay model. Garment/vessel/model starter batches are limited to 1 output and quality 1, with the normal access fee plus 2 dr supervision. Each specialty can complete its own foundation proof.

rules.title: Controlled making
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 supervised starter-production jobs in any material line, each in a distinct work year, with paid inputs, reconciled output and at least 1 sellable result.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock independent basic production: garment batch cap 2, vessel cap 4 and clay-model cap 2, quality cap 1. Remove the 2 dr supervision fee. Unlock optional inspection: +1 quality for 3 dr/batch, still limited by the learned quality cap.

rules.title: Garment assembly
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 basic-garment work years, each producing at least 1 quality-1 garment from paid materials.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock fitted-garment method, quality cap 2; garment batch limit becomes 4.

rules.title: Patterns and dyes
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 quality-2 garment batches; each must reconcile cloth/thread consumption.
rules.rewardDescription: Garment quality cap becomes 3. Unlock dyed garments: 1 pigment/garment for +1 recipe quality before cap, base ask 130 dr; dye/colour-specific orders check actual pigment use.

rules.title: Tailoring fit
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 inspected quality-2 garment orders; all units must meet the quoted specification.
rules.rewardDescription: Garment quality cap becomes 3; batch limit 6. Unlock fit/finish commissions with explicit quoted payment.

rules.title: Batch cutting
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 quality-3 garment batches of at least 4 units each.
rules.rewardDescription: Garment batch limit becomes 8. For batches of at least 4, total base cloth requirement becomes ceil(recipe cloth units * quantity * 7 / 8), applied to the actual recipe base cloth requirement; thread and pigment unchanged.

rules.title: Fine finishing
rules.proofDescription: Deliver 2 quality-3 garment contracts on time, with recorded payment and no unpaid supplier balance.
rules.rewardDescription: Garment quality cap becomes 4; batch limit 10. Unlock ceremonial garment recipe.

rules.title: Masterwork tailoring
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 registered masterwork assessment over 2 work years: 4 quality-4 ceremonial garments in total, fully paid inputs and accepted inspection.
rules.rewardDescription: Garment quality cap becomes 5; batch limit 12. Qualify for Master Tailor career offers; unlock repair/restoration contracts. No cash awarded solely for learning.

rules.title: Vessel forming
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 fired-vessel production years with at least 1 quality-1 sellable vessel each.
rules.rewardDescription: Vessel quality cap 2; batch limit 6.

rules.title: Controlled firing
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 quality-2 fired-vessel batches with fuel and kiln fees recorded.
rules.rewardDescription: Vessel quality cap becomes 3. Unlock controlled firing: consume 1 extra fuel per 4 vessels (round up) for +1 recipe quality before cap; vessel batch limit 8.

rules.title: Form and decoration
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 inspected quality-2 vessel orders.
rules.rewardDescription: Vessel quality cap 3; batch limit 10. Unlock decorated vessels, consuming 1 pigment per 4 vessels (round up).

rules.title: Kiln batching
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 quality-3 batches of at least 8 vessels.
rules.rewardDescription: Batch limit 12; base fuel becomes ceil(vessels / 2), replacing 1 fuel/vessel. Controlled-firing extra fuel remains payable.

rules.title: Reliable ceramic sets
rules.proofDescription: Deliver 2 quality-3 matched-set contracts on time with reconciled materials.
rules.rewardDescription: Vessel quality cap 4; batch limit 14. Unlock matched sets with a minimum-quality contract check, not automatic extra retail demand.

rules.title: Master ceramic work
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 registered assessment over 2 work years: 12 quality-4 decorated vessels in total, including 1 accepted matched set.
rules.rewardDescription: Vessel quality cap 5; batch limit 16. Qualify for Master Potter career offers; unlock large commission bids.

rules.title: Modelling and relief
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 clay-model job and 1 wood-relief practice job after A4; both record paid materials.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock small relief recipe, sculpture quality cap 2; maximum 2 small pieces per work year.

rules.title: Stone cutting
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 quality-2 relief production jobs with measured material use.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock stone figurines; 1 stone block + 1 timber support per figurine, maximum 2/year; tool rental 8 dr/work year.

rules.title: Proportion and likeness
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 inspected quality-2 stone-figure jobs.
rules.rewardDescription: Sculpture quality cap 3. Unlock portrait/bust recipe, maximum 1/year.

rules.title: Large-work planning
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 quality-3 bust and 1 reconciled project budget.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock 2-work-year large relief projects; inputs reserved at start, progress resumes after interruption without duplicating output.

rules.title: Commission execution
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 quality-3 large relief project on its agreed work-year deadline; account for every input and payment.
rules.rewardDescription: Sculpture quality cap 4. Unlock monumental-work assessment; the assessment contract is routinely offered when eligible.

rules.title: Masterwork sculpture
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 registered quality-4 monument assessment over 2 work years, with paid materials and accepted measurement/finish review.
rules.rewardDescription: Sculpture quality cap 5. Qualify for Master Sculptor career offers; unlock monumental/restoration commissions.

rules.title: Reading and questioning
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 guided reading/discussion session; record a question and its stated evidence.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock guided philosophy practice: 1 papyrus + 1 ink + 2 dr teaching fee per work year.

rules.title: Reasoned argument
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 argument exercise with a claim, 2 recorded reasons, 1 counterargument and a response.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock structured debate activities; each completed ordinary debate grants +3 Philosophy and +2 Oratory, once per work year.

rules.title: Evidence and comparison
rules.proofDescription: Compare two actual records and record their agreement or disagreement in two distinct comparison records.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock comparison records and fact-checking tasks. Claims are evaluated against recorded world/exercise data, not a random approval roll.

rules.title: Inquiry and ethics
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 reviewed inquiry and 1 reasoned public dilemma exercise. Review checks evidence/process, not a required moral stance.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock research and civic specializations; qualify for Philosopher/tutor career offers and paid copying work from finite payer budgets.

rules.title: Systematic observation
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 observation projects in different work years, using distinct recorded data.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock paid observation-record contracts: base fee 20 dr; each project consumes 1 papyrus and 1 ink.

rules.title: Measurement and calculation
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 measurement exercises within 2% of the stated reference, with calculations retained.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock surveys and calculations: base fee 40 dr/project; 2 papyrus + 1 ink + 5 dr instrument rental.

rules.title: Testable explanations
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 explanation stating its predicted result before observing the outcome; compare it with recorded results.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock planned field investigations and competing explanations; accepted investigation base fee 60 dr, costing 2 papyrus + 2 ink + 5 dr instrument rental.

rules.title: Independent checking
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 checked investigations in different work years; an ordinary NPC reviewer reproduces its recorded results within 2%.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock reviewed-method contracts: base fee 90 dr; investigation inputs plus 5 dr review fee. Reviewer access is regular, never a named-figure lottery.

rules.title: Research synthesis
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 synthesis of at least 3 earlier distinct records spanning 2 years, with 2 independently checked results.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock 2-work-year treatise projects: base fee 180 dr on acceptance, total 4 papyrus + 3 ink + 10 dr instrument/review fees.

rules.title: Original inquiry
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 registered 2-work-year original-inquiry assessment: predeclared question, 2 distinct results, independent check and a defensible conclusion, including a valid negative finding.
rules.rewardDescription: Qualify for Scientist career offers; unlock leading a funded research project, whose complete fee and material budget are quoted before acceptance.

rules.title: Public speaking
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 public addresses on different local issues, each citing 2 recorded facts and 1 explicit trade-off.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock civic hearing work: base fee 20 dr, 1 papyrus + 1 ink/project; completed competent service adds +2 district reputation.

rules.title: Negotiation
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 agreements where each party has the offered stock/cash and accepts the recorded terms.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock mediation contracts: base fee 40 dr, 1 papyrus + 1 ink/project; fulfilled agreements add +3 district reputation.

rules.title: Public accounts
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 public budget with all money/materials reconciled and 1 completed service within that budget.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock administration contracts: base fee 60 dr, 2 papyrus + 1 ink/project; public funds remain a separate ledger, never personal cash. Successful service adds +4 reputation.

rules.title: Coalition building
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 agreements involving at least 2 distinct local groups; fulfill the recorded commitments.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock multi-party civic projects: base fee 90 dr, 2 papyrus + 2 ink/project; fulfilled projects add +4 reputation and record which groups benefited.

rules.title: Policy and consequences
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 2-work-year policy project with declared costs, affected groups and 1 follow-up evaluation against actual outcomes.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock policy proposals and their before/after public ledger preview: base fee 180 dr, 4 papyrus + 3 ink total; fulfilled, evaluated service adds +5 reputation.

rules.title: Statesmanship
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 registered civic assessment: present a funded plan, secure an agreement, deliver it and reconcile the public account across 2 work years. District reputation at least 60.
rules.rewardDescription: Qualify for Politician career offers; unlock seeking public office and proposing district policy. Appointment needs an available funded role; learning grants neither public money nor automatic office.

rules.title: Measures and exchange
rules.proofDescription: Complete 1 supervised stock-counting job or recorded purchase/sale with correct quantity and payment.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock counting practice and a simple lot ledger. Prices, totals and ordinary market access are already visible without this node.

rules.title: Cost accounting
rules.proofDescription: Reconcile 1 paid material basket: cash spent equals item quantities at their accepted quotes plus explicit fees.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock cost basis per lot and gross-margin previews using the current buyer quote; no guarantee of a future sale price.

rules.title: Price comparison
rules.proofDescription: Record 3 actual item quotes across at least 2 market years and compare each against a recorded acquisition cost.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock bid/ask target plans for the existing annual market visit; plans cannot spend missing cash or trade with missing stock.

rules.title: Inventory planning
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 distinct annual stock reconciliations with recorded purchases, sales, consumption and remaining inventory.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock item-by-item stock targets and costed replenishment plans. Basic baskets remain accessible; replenishment is not an extra market visit.

rules.title: Commercial production planning
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 costed supply plans using either farm output or artisan products; source every input and fulfill the stated output/delivery.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock demand-led production and purchase plans that compare actual material cost, labour, stock and buyer budget. Farming yield and artisan recipes still require their own skills.

rules.title: Negotiated supply
rules.proofDescription: Fulfill 2 pre-agreed, funded fixed-price orders. Orders are distinct work-year jobs; introductory fixed-price delivery work is available before this node.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock counteroffers within 10% of the posted reference price in return for quantity or lead-time terms; the NPC acceptance bounds, budget and stock are explicit. No automatic price premium.

rules.title: Delivery logistics
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 paid delivery work years within the agreed work-year deadline, with cargo and fees reconciled.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock scheduled deliveries with at most 2 item lines; baseline haulage is 12 dr/order and quantities stay within the market and carrier limits shown before acceptance. Delivery consumes the work action and existing visit; it adds neither a free visit nor unearned soldier capability.

rules.title: Stock turnover
rules.proofDescription: Complete 2 trading work years with non-negative realized gross margin, actual paid receipts and reconciled closing stock.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock repeat restock/sale plans with user-set cash and quantity caps. Every execution remains subject to current quotes, finite demand and the annual visit budget.

rules.title: Enterprise accounts
rules.proofDescription: Deliver 2 funded contracts with itemized supplier costs, access/transport fees, final payment and closing stock; no unpaid supplier amount.
rules.rewardDescription: Unlock quoted 2-work-year supply contracts and their cash-flow preview. Payer reserves payment; player does not receive the full future payment in advance.

rules.title: Commercial stewardship
rules.proofDescription: Complete a 2-work-year assessment delivering 2 funded orders to 2 distinct buyer accounts; reconcile cash, stock, fees and commitments in both years.
rules.rewardDescription: Qualify for Merchant or Trading-house manager career offers. Unlock an integrated 2-year stock/order/delivery plan within the existing action and visit limits; this grants no free goods, price immunity or personal ownership of employer funds.

figurePaths.name: Alexander the Great
figurePaths.summary: Enter through campaign service while Alexander is in Egypt. Logistics, command and a completed strategic operation matter; an age-28 General appointment is not an entry requirement.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Alexander

encounter.location: Egypt, then the Macedonian campaign train

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Alexander the Great's work

stages.title: Campaign Stores Aide
stages.description: A checked tally of a small stores issue establishes useful entry-level campaign work.

stages.title: Campaign Provisioner
stages.description: A delivered, itemised supply assignment is a contribution; merely joining the army is not.

stages.title: Campaign Staff Officer
stages.description: Repeated staff work must reconcile provisions, routes and the agreed operational task.

stages.title: Trusted Campaign Commander
stages.description: Sustained responsibility for real operations distinguishes a senior subordinate from an observer.

capstone.title: Alexander the Great
capstone.description: A separate funded campaign programme and strategic result support the figure-defining legacy. A title or royal birth alone does not.

figurePaths.name: Aristotle
figurePaths.summary: Start with argument and observation at the Lyceum, then build reviewed inquiry and teaching. Later work continues through the Aristotelian school and makes no claim of a dead teacher's personal endorsement.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Aristotle
Aristotle: Nicomachean Ethics

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Aristotle's work

stages.title: Inquiry Note Keeper
stages.description: An organised and checked set of inquiry notes assists the school before independent comparison is attempted.

stages.title: Lyceum Copyist
stages.description: An annotated comparison is useful work, rather than attendance at a lecture.

stages.title: Lyceum Researcher
stages.description: Two seasons connect claims to observations and preserve disagreements for review.

stages.title: Peripatetic Scholar
stages.description: The contribution joins research, criticism and teaching; tutoring a ruler is not a substitute.

capstone.title: Aristotle, the philosopher and naturalist
capstone.description: The resulting body of inquiry and teaching, built on research mastery, earns the philosophical legacy. Post-322 work is explicitly a continuation of the school.

figurePaths.name: Euclid
figurePaths.summary: Join the geometrical tradition associated with the Elements around 300 BCE. The path rewards justified constructions and a coherent deductive collection, without inventing a Museum appointment or a precise death date.

sources.title: University of St Andrews: Euclid
Clark University: Elements, Book I

encounter.location: A geometrical teaching circle in Alexandria; a personal meeting is uncertain

stages.title: Diagram Aide
stages.description: A labelled, checked elementary diagram provides a first practical contribution to geometrical study.

stages.title: Geometrical Copyist
stages.description: Careful copying includes the reasons behind the diagram, not merely a finished picture.

stages.title: Proof Checker
stages.description: Two seasons of checking expose assumptions and repair errors before a demonstration is accepted.

stages.title: Geometer of the Teaching Circle
stages.description: A deductive sequence must retain definitions, earlier results and independent review.

capstone.title: Euclid, the geometer
capstone.description: An enduring organisation of demonstrated results supports Euclid's legacy; the route does not claim every theorem was first discovered by its compiler.

figurePaths.name: Lysippos
figurePaths.summary: Develop measured models, portrait proportions and bronze workshop projects. Stone sculpture is useful training, but cannot alone establish Lysippos's distinctive bronze achievement.

sources.title: Getty Research Institute: Lysippos
Vatican Museums: Apoxyomenos
The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Pergamon and the Hellenistic Kingdoms of the Ancient World

encounter.location: A Greek bronze workshop following Lysippan practice

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Lysippos's work

stages.title: Bronze Workshop Aide
stages.description: Prepared materials and a checked small study support the workshop before a complete measured model is undertaken.

stages.title: Bronze Workshop Assistant
stages.description: A model records pose and proportions for the bronze workshop.

stages.title: Portrait Modeller
stages.description: The work uses actual bronze and fuel; a stone figurine is not silently relabelled a bronze.

stages.title: Master of Lysippan Form
stages.description: Several seasons of models, casting work and revision form the senior workshop contribution.

capstone.title: Lysippos of Sikyon, the sculptor
capstone.description: Sculptural mastery must be applied to real bronze projects and measured form. No literary treatise is invented for Lysippos.

figurePaths.name: Pytheas of Massalia
figurePaths.summary: Prepare an expedition, collect navigational observations and deliver a checked voyage account. The route preserves uncertainty about the lost work and the identity of Thule.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press: Pytheas of Massalia
Cambridge University Press: Geography in Pseudo-Aristotle's De Mundo

encounter.location: Massalia and an Atlantic expedition; the voyage is dated approximately

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Pytheas of Massalia's work

stages.title: Expedition Provisioner
stages.description: Paid preparation and a working log are a genuine expedition contribution.

stages.title: Navigation Observer
stages.description: Observations are compared across seasons rather than granting a discovery for one conversation.

stages.title: Keeper of the Northern Voyage Log
stages.description: The substantial contribution is the retained, tested account and its safe delivery; it does not settle every later geographical identification.

capstone.title: Pytheas of Massalia, the navigator
capstone.description: The navigational body of work earns an Epic legacy. It neither proves a particular identification of Thule nor promotes Pytheas to Legendary.

figurePaths.name: Menander
figurePaths.summary: Write, revise, rehearse and stage comedy about human situations. Political office and scientific mastery do not substitute for dramatic achievement.

sources.title: Oxford Classical Dictionary: Menander, leading writer of New Comedy
The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Theater in Ancient Greece
Getty Museum: Portrait Bust of Menander

encounter.location: The Athenian stage and a New Comedy rehearsal company

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Menander's work

stages.title: Rehearsal Aide
stages.description: Usable scene copies and checked rehearsal cues support a performance before revising a dramatic scene.

stages.title: Stage Copyist
stages.description: A usable dramatic scene and rehearsal notes build on the initial rehearsal contribution.

stages.title: New Comedy Collaborator
stages.description: The text must be tried in performance and revised through repeated work.

stages.title: Dramatist of New Comedy
stages.description: Several seasons of completed writing and staging distinguish a dramatist from an eloquent speaker.

capstone.title: Menander, the comic playwright
capstone.description: A substantial dramatic body of work supports the Legendary legacy. Music may support rehearsal, but no unimplemented performance mastery is required.

figurePaths.name: Demetrius the Besieger
figurePaths.summary: An authored service encounter after the Gaza campaign leaves enough years to prepare real siege works. Machinery and a negotiated settlement remain Epic; only successful alternate-history capture of Rhodes supports Legendary.

sources.title: Oxford University Press: The Great Siege of Rhodes
Oxford University Press: The Young Demetrius Poliorcetes
Plutarch: Life of Demetrius, Internet Classics Archive

encounter.location: Eastern Mediterranean campaign workshops, then the siege of Rhodes

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Demetrius the Besieger's work

stages.title: Siege Workshop Assistant
stages.description: Early work establishes a real engineering contribution, without claiming a victory.

stages.title: Siege Engineer
stages.description: Two seasons of construction and revision establish engineering responsibility.

stages.title: Director of Siege Works
stages.description: Senior contribution requires delivered projects and operational accounting, not merely impressive plans.

capstone.title: Demetrius the Besieger
capstone.description: The completed siege programme earns the Epic figure title. A separate one-shot Rhodes resolution can raise it only on actual alternate-history capture.

legendaryContribution.title: Distinguished Director of Siege Works
legendaryContribution.traditionTitle: Distinguished Custodian of Demetrian Siege Methods
legendaryContribution.description: The senior contribution receives Epic recognition only after Demetrius the Besieger's successful Legendary achievement. Earlier Rare contributions remain separately recorded.

figurePaths.name: Theophrastus
figurePaths.summary: Treat Aristotle's colleague and successor as an investigator in his own right. Comparative plant observations, seasons and a reviewed botanical account define the route.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Theophrastus

encounter.location: The Lyceum and its comparative botanical work in Athens

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Theophrastus's work

stages.title: Plant Records Assistant
stages.description: A real comparative record starts the botanical contribution.

stages.title: Comparative Plant Investigator
stages.description: Repeated comparison matters more than merely collecting names.

stages.title: Peripatetic Botanical Scholar
stages.description: A sustained botanical contribution reflects Theophrastus's independent research and school leadership.

capstone.title: Theophrastus, the naturalist
capstone.description: The independent botanical account earns an Epic legacy under the strict agreed standard; it does not automatically become Legendary.

figurePaths.name: Zeno of Citium
figurePaths.summary: Develop argument, ethical inquiry and public teaching. Zeno remains Epic unless an independently functioning Stoic school is actually established through a separate funded programme.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Stoicism
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Ancient Political Philosophy
Diogenes Laertius, Book VII: Lives of the Stoics, Fordham Internet History Sourcebooks

encounter.location: The Athenian Stoa and its ethical teaching

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Zeno of Citium's work

stages.title: Student of the Stoa
stages.description: A defensible contribution goes beyond attendance or assent.

stages.title: Stoic Discussion Leader
stages.description: Repeated teaching must answer objections and preserve its reasons.

stages.title: Scholar of Stoic Ethics
stages.description: An independent body of inquiry is a major contribution, while founding a school remains a separate outcome.

capstone.title: Zeno of Citium
capstone.description: This body of ethical inquiry earns the Epic figure title. The working Legendary interpretation requires a functioning school, not an announcement.

promotion.title: Zeno of Citium, founder of a Stoic school

legendaryContribution.title: Distinguished Scholar of Stoic Ethics
legendaryContribution.traditionTitle: Distinguished Custodian of Early Stoic Inquiry
legendaryContribution.description: The senior contribution receives Epic recognition only after Zeno of Citium's successful Legendary achievement. Earlier Rare contributions remain separately recorded.

figurePaths.name: Ptolemy I Soter
figurePaths.summary: Build audited administration, supply and political support before attempting a durable independent hereditary government. Becoming satrap, gaining wealth or reaching 305 BCE does not found a dynasty by itself.

sources.title: University of Canterbury: Ptolemy's Divine Alexander coin
Cambridge University Press: Alexander historical sources, excerpt
Andrew Erskine: Culture and Power in Ptolemaic Egypt

encounter.location: Egyptian administration and the emerging Ptolemaic court

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Ptolemy I Soter's work

stages.title: Egyptian Administration Clerk
stages.description: A completed account is useful work; holding an administrative title is insufficient.

stages.title: Ptolemaic Supply Commissioner
stages.description: Two seasons connect administration to actual funded delivery.

stages.title: Steward of Egyptian Government
stages.description: A major contribution combines operating accounts with workable institutions and support.

capstone.title: Ptolemy I Soter
capstone.description: Completed administration supports Ptolemy's Epic title. A separate successful founding outcome is required for the Ptolemaic dynasty and Legendary promotion.

promotion.title: Ptolemy I Soter, founder of the Ptolemaic dynasty

legendaryContribution.title: Distinguished Steward of Egyptian Government
legendaryContribution.traditionTitle: Distinguished Custodian of Early Ptolemaic Statecraft
legendaryContribution.description: The senior contribution receives Epic recognition only after Ptolemy I Soter's successful Legendary achievement. Earlier Rare contributions remain separately recorded.

figurePaths.name: Cleomenes of Naucratis
figurePaths.summary: Develop actual grain accounts, deliveries and revenue oversight. Ancient accounts of Cleomenes are hostile; humane relief choices are authored alternatives, not a proven benevolent historical policy.

sources.title: Oxford Classical Dictionary: Cleomenes of Naucratis, financial administrator
Marc Mendoza: Cleomenes of Naucratis, reality, sources and historiography
Georges Le Rider: Cleomene de Naucratis

encounter.location: Egyptian revenue offices and the grain administration

tradition.location: Later schools, workshops and surviving accounts of Cleomenes of Naucratis's work

stages.title: Revenue Records Assistant
stages.description: A genuine balanced account starts the contribution.

stages.title: Grain Supply Auditor
stages.description: Repeated delivery and accounting show impact beyond a wealthy balance sheet.

stages.title: Steward of Egyptian Grain Accounts
stages.description: The senior contribution requires actual supply and public accounting; coercion is not silently praised as relief.

capstone.title: Cleomenes of Naucratis, the financial administrator
capstone.description: The completed administrative body of work earns an Epic legacy. Wealth alone and invented benevolence do not qualify.
